_note: Newest first. Each entry: a unique id (date and a word), a date, a title and a sentence or two in plain words for players and teachers. The app shows entries a device has not seen yet.

entries.title: Five new games and a new look
items: Five new 3D games: Summit Scramble, Spot Kick, Lantern Rally, Tower Together and Glim Garden. Each also plays with 3D off.
Every game has its own picture now, and the lobby, questions and podium have been redrawn. Teachers can choose a backdrop for the big screen.
Three new kinds of question: polls, fill in the blanks and sort into groups.

entries.title: For teachers and schools
items: Lessons: run several games, slides and discussion questions in one room, with the same players.
Reports that show the wrong answer a class shared, who may need a hand, and how a set or a student is doing over time.
Classes: logins for students with no email, groups, co-teachers and a gradebook.
For a school's own copy: houses, house points, cups and tournaments.

entries.title: For players
items: My mistakes keeps the questions you got wrong so you can fix them, and there is a new challenge every day.
Challenge a friend, play on your own against practice bots, and choose which reactions are on your bar.
A page for every Glim, saved outfits, a wishlist and badges for what you have earned.

entries.title: Ludora for everyone
items: Read aloud: a speaker button reads each question and its answers, and teachers can have the big screen read them too.
Teachers can give chosen students extra time, in any room or once for a whole class. Nobody else can tell.
Comfort settings in every game: hide the timer, calm mode, colour-safe answer tiles, bigger buttons, captions for sounds and a buzz when your answer goes in.
Answer with the keyboard: 1 to 4 or A to D.
An easier-to-read typeface, wider spacing, the highest contrast and less transparency in Settings, which now has a search.
Install Ludora as an app, and sign in on a shared computer without staying signed in.

entries.title: Hosting a live game
items: Room settings, a QR code to join, a brain break, add time, a quiet room and your phone as a remote control.
Three new question types: polls, fill in the blanks, and sort into groups.
